plan.approachName: Prepare-on-1.9, then one atomic swap, then small legal-scope fixes (incremental safety)
principles: Green after every commit: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm build:demo must pass on every commit of the migration branch; runtime smoke (pnpm dev) is the per-epic gate.

Do the read-your-own-write redesigns BEFORE the swap, on solid-js 1.9.12, as pure refactors: producers return their computed values, consumers never re-read state they just wrote, store guards move inside the draft. On 1.9 the synchronous runtime is the safety net (behavior must be identical), and after the swap the code is already deferred-write-correct.

Exactly one commit is allowed to be non-incremental: the dependency/config/import swap (E2-1). Everything that can be moved out of it (dead code, geometry threading, setup pipeline, mirrors, shared demo helper) is moved out; a demo-only compat shim (Index/onMount/batch/produce) keeps the 20 @ts-nocheck demos out of that commit entirely.

Smallest correct change first, idiomatic end state second: createContext(null) before any context redesign; flush() at the mouseup gesture-commit boundary (legal scope) as the public-callback guarantee even though geometry is already threaded; storePath only in ShowcaseDemo's flat primitive-field config stores, never where a Set/Map/Date lives in a store.

flush() legality is scope-dependent and is written into every issue that uses it: LEGAL in event handlers, timers, promise continuations, test bodies; SILENT NO-OP inside createEffect apply; THROWS inside onSettled/createTrackedEffect. Never prescribe flush() in the last two.

Signals vs stores differ under createRoot: store setters are legal inside createRoot bodies, plain signal setters throw. Tests for signal-only stores keep writes outside the root body; tests never wrap writes in createRoot to 'fix' them.
Every callback handed to onSettled/createEffect apply or crossing a component boundary gets a block body (Setter<T> returns the new value and rc.6 throws on non-function returns).

Built-ins inside a store are replace-only; prefer a signal holding an immutable collection (taskStore.collapsedTasks, resourceStore.collapsedGroups, selectionStore.selectedIds already do this). The one broken member (ganttConfigStore.expandedTasks) moves to that shape.
One issue -> one commit -> one push, each independently revertable; dist-demo/ refresh is its own final chore commit; no scope creep without an explicit decision issue.
plan.branchStrategy: Create a long-lived feature branch `solid-2` from main (main stays releasable on 1.9.12 throughout). Every issue lands as exactly one commit on `solid-2` and is pushed immediately (`git push origin solid-2`), matching the gantt-6jw convention. E0 and E1 commits are runtime-neutral refactors on 1.9.12 and could be cherry-picked to main if the migration stalls (they are bug-fix-quality on their own). E2-1 is the only commit that cannot be split. After E6-5 (dist-demo refresh) merge `solid-2` into main with a merge commit (not squash, so per-issue reverts stay possible) and only then consider a `release` push (publish.yml triggers on that branch). Do not delete `solid-2` until the first stable-line re-bump (E7-5) has landed.
plan.versionPolicy: During the RC line pin EXACT versions (no caret): solid-js 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/web 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.38, @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2 (moved to devDependencies), jsdom ^25 (caret is fine, not part of the RC line), optionally @solidjs/testing-library 1.0.0-beta.3 and @solidjs/diagnostics 2.0.0-rc.6 (exact). Rationale: rc-to-rc changes have altered write-guard semantics and plugin posture already; an accidental minor bump inside a caret range would invalidate the audit. Add "engines": { "node": ">=20.19" } to package.json to match the plugin. Re-bump is a dedicated follow-up issue (E7-5): bump all four together, re-run the full verification plan, and relax solid-js/@solidjs/web to ^2.0.0 only once 2.0.0 stable is published; at that point also decide peerDependencies. Keep the lockfile committed in the same commit as any bump.

epics.title: Pre-flight on 1.9.12: decisions, tooling globs, dead code, callback bodies, shared demo helper
epics.goal: Make every later commit smaller and verifiable: record the decisions the migration depends on, make config files visible to the quality gates, delete code the audit proved dead, and normalize the patterns (callback block bodies, five copy-pasted lifecycle bodies, seven self-reading latches) that would otherwise be converted five times.
epics.rationale: All of these are runtime-neutral on 1.9.12 and verifiable with today's dev server, so they carry zero migration risk and shrink the one non-incremental commit (E2-1). The tooling-globs item is a prerequisite for the swap commit to be checked by any gate at all (digest-t1 tooling critic: every tooling file this migration edits is invisible to every quality gate).
epics.verificationGate: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm prettier-check && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm build:demo; pnpm dev smoke: examples/gantt.html, examples/perf.html, examples/showcase.html render and drag works (unchanged behavior).

epics.title: Read-your-own-write redesigns as pure refactors on 1.9.12
epics.goal: Rewrite every write-then-read-back seam the tracer found (chains A, B, C, D, F, G, I, J1, J2, J3) so producers return values and consumers never re-read what they just wrote, while the synchronous 1.9 runtime still guarantees identical behavior and today's tests and demos verify it.
epics.rationale: These are the genuinely structural items of the migration (digest tracer verdict: setup pipeline and gesture-commit boundary). Doing them on 1.9 turns them from 'migration fixes verified only by reasoning about deferred writes' into 'refactors verified by existing behavior', and it removes produce/path-setter usage from the store layer so E2-1 becomes a literal body move. Chain A fails closed (blank chart, no error) and chain H persists stale data, so both must be correct before the swap ever runs the chart.
epics.verificationGate: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm build:demo; pnpm dev smoke on examples/gantt.html (first paint has bars, view-mode switch regenerates columns), showcase.html (drag/resize/progress/presets), constraint.html (cascade), box-select.html, db.html with pnpm dev:server (drag persists exact final position; reload shows it).

children.title: taskStore: delete-in-draft removeTask, guard-inside-draft + leaf-mutation updateBarPosition/batchMovePositions, patchTask, explicit-id collapseAllTasks, strengthened gantt-6hx guard
children.description: taskStore.ts:134 `setTasks(id, undefined)` relies on the 1.x delete idiom that keeps the key in 2.0 -> `setTasks(produce(s => { delete s[id]; }))` now (literal draft body after the swap). taskStore.ts:108 `if (!tasks[id]) return;` reads committed state outside the draft -> delete it; the produce body at :112-113 already checks the draft. taskStore.ts:114-117 and :165-168 replace the whole task object to defeat a 1.x memo identity check (gantt-6hx cause #1); rewrite both to leaf mutation (`for (const k in position) if (position[k] !== undefined) task._bar[k] = position[k]` and `task._bar.x = originalX + deltaX`) — digest lib-stores-task measured that leaf mutation invalidates only the _bar.x subscriber on rc.6 and Bar.tsx:175-187 already reads leaves. Make batchMovePositions RETURN `Map<string, {x:number,width:number}>` of the positions it wrote (it has them at :167) for E1-4. Add `patchTask(id, patch: Partial<ProcessedTask>)` implemented as `setTasks(produce(s => { const t = s[id]; if (t) Object.assign(t, patch); }))` and switch useBarDrag.ts:250-256 to `deps.taskStore.patchTask(t.id, { progress: newProgress })` (whole-node replacement from a pre-write snapshot clobbers staged _bar writes). collapseAllTasks (:232-243) takes an optional `ids?: string[]`; when given, use it instead of scanning Object.values(tasks). In tests/taskStore.test.ts:84-103 add the negative half of the guard: a second memo `nameRuns` over `store.tasks['t1']?.name` whose run count must stay 1 after updateBarPosition (this is the only mechanism preventing someone from porting the object-replacement shape into the draft). Keep tests L72-81 (taskCount across add/remove/clear) as the delete-vs-undefined guard.
acceptance: pnpm test: taskStore suite passes including the new `nameRuns === 1` assertion on 1.9.12.
pnpm dev examples/showcase.html and gantt.html: drag, resize, progress drag update visually at 60fps (no regression of gantt-6hx).

children.title: ganttConfigStore: expandedTasks -> signal-held immutable Set, makeSetter reads prev inside the update, retype setters to void
children.description: ganttConfigStore.ts:146 holds a Set inside createStore and :172-203 mutate it in place via produce; rc.6 does not proxy built-in collections so expand/collapse would notify nothing (Gantt.tsx:371 rowLayouts and useTaskVirtualization.ts:161 go dead). Per decision E0-1, move it OUT of the store: `const [expandedTasks, setExpandedTasks] = createSignal<ReadonlySet<string>>(new Set(options.expandedTasks || []))`, remove the field from GanttConfigState (:54), reimplement toggleTaskExpansion/expandTask/collapseTask/expandAllTasks/collapseAllTasks as functional updaters that build a NEW Set (`setExpandedTasks(prev => { const n = new Set(prev); n.has(id) ? n.delete(id) : n.add(id); return n; })`), delete the committed-read guards at :186 and :196 (a replace-based updater is idempotent), and keep the accessor at :304 and getConfig at :280 (Array.from(expandedTasks())). Also updateOptions (:214-257) must set expandedTasks via the signal when present. makeSetter (:151-166): move the updater invocation into the store's own updater form `setState(key, (prev) => typeof value === 'function' ? value(prev) : value)` and return the locally computed next value rather than re-reading `state[key]` (:164). Change the 20 public setter types (:81-100) from `Setter<T>` to `(v: T | ((prev: T) => T)) => void` — grep shows no in-repo caller uses a return value (only ganttSetup.ts:69-73 and BarDemo.tsx:195 call them). Add a comment on GanttConfigState that ganttStart/ganttEnd/ignoredDates are unproxied Dates and must be replaced, never mutated. `setExpandedTasks` in the public interface becomes the signal setter.
acceptance: pnpm typecheck passes with the retyped setters (fix any caller that relied on a return value — expected: none).

children.title: Setup pipeline: generateDates(start,end,step,unit), setupDates/changeViewMode return the window, ganttSetup computes config and resourceIndexMap locally

Give initializeTasks an optional `window` parameter so Gantt's view-mode path can pass the window changeViewMode returned (used in E3-1). Fix Gantt.tsx:515 truthiness guard to `firstTask?._bar?.x !== undefined`. Add to tests/ganttSetup.test.ts: after initializeTasks on fresh stores every task has `_resourceIndex >= 0`, `_isHidden === false`, and `_bar.x` derived from its start date (not from `new Date()`), and dates().length > 0.

children.title: Gesture-commit boundary: thread applied geometry/progress from onDragMove into onDragEnd, onResizeEnd(taskId, geom), resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx, geom)

Make onDragMove record what it wrote and onDragEnd use that: in useBarDrag.ts set `data['lastGeom'] = { x, width }` in each write branch (:164 `{x:newX, width: originalWidth}`, :196-199 `{x:newX, width:newWidth}`, :208 `{x: originalX, width:newWidth}`, batch path :149 from the Map batchMovePositions now returns) and `data['finalProgress'] = newProgress` at :252; in onDragEnd (:260-283) use `data['lastGeom'] ?? {x: deps.x(), width: deps.width()}` for onDateChange and `data['finalProgress'] ?? t.progress` for onProgressChange; delete the comment at :270. Widen the contract: `onResizeEnd?: (taskId: string, geom?: {x:number; width:number}) => void` in GanttEventHandlers (GanttEvents.tsx:7/16/36), Bar props, TaskLayer props and Gantt.tsx:481; `resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx, geom?)` (taskLayerConstraints.ts:83-105) uses `geom ?? ctx.taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId)`; TaskLayer.handleResizeEnd (:98-102) forwards geom; Bar.tsx:300-302 keyboard resize passes `{ x: x(), width: newWidth }`; SummaryBar.tsx:146-150 passes the summary's final position from the Map returned by batchMovePositions (stash it in `data` at :142). children.title: useGanttScroll takes the containerApi accessor; container passes measured dimensions as data
children.description: Showstopper (b) and chain I: useGanttScroll.handleContainerReady creates six effects inside the onContainerReady callback, which fires from GanttContainer's onMount (children-forbidden after the swap). Invert the API now: `useGanttScroll(containerApi: Accessor<ContainerAPILike | null>)` declares `scrollLeft/scrollTop/viewportWidth/viewportHeight = createMemo(() => containerApi()?.<x>Signal?.() ?? 0)` at hook top level; delete handleContainerReady (:50-98) and its interface member (:35-36); Gantt.tsx:248 becomes `useGanttScroll(containerApi)` and :491 is deleted. In GanttContainer.tsx:170-202 add plain numbers `containerWidth: scrollAreaRef.clientWidth, containerHeight: scrollAreaRef.clientHeight` to the api object and seed `setViewportHeight(scrollAreaRef.clientHeight)` alongside setContainerWidth at :172; Gantt.tsx:494-497 'today' scroll uses `api.containerWidth` instead of `api.getContainerWidth()`. Add a doc comment on `onContainerReady` (GanttContainer.tsx:75) stating that it will run inside a children-forbidden scope: store the api in a signal, never create primitives or call onCleanup inside. After E0-3 the file is ~40 lines.

children.title: Virtualization: tracked grouping memo (shared helper) instead of count-keyed caches; pool counters via memo prev; explicit expandedTasks dependency
children.description: useTaskVirtualization.ts:70-96 and its copy TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:45-73 invalidate only when the key COUNT changes; under coalesced flushes a same-tick add+remove leaves the grouping permanently stale (chain G). Extract `groupTasksByResource(tasks: Record<string, ProcessedTask|undefined>, keys: string[])` into a pure helper and make each consumer `const tasksByResource = createMemo(() => { const t = props.taskStore?.tasks; if (!t) return new Map(); const keys = Object.keys(t); /* tracked via ownKeys */ return untrack(() => groupTasksByResource(t, keys)); })`. Pool high-water counters (:201-232) become `createMemo((prev) => ..., [])`-style derivations from prev length rather than closure mutation (1.9 supports the prev argument; keep it 1-arg-compatible for E2-1). splitTaskIds (:150-198) reads isTaskExpanded inside untrack; read `props.ganttConfig?.expandedTasks?.()` once OUTSIDE the untrack so the memo subscribes to the new signal from E1-2.

children.title: Gantt.tsx: split every effect into compute/apply; plain prevViewMode; onReady deferred via queueMicrotask
children.description: Six effects write from their compute (all throw in rc.6 dev; untrack does not clear the owner). Selection (:184-188): `createEffect(() => [...selectionStore.selectedIds()], (ids) => { props.onSelectionChange?.(new Set(ids)); })` — compute returns a plain array so apply never reads a proxy. Setup (:290-304): `createEffect(() => { const tasks = effectiveTasks(); resourceStore.collapsedGroups(); taskStore.collapsedTasks(); return tasks; }, (tasks) => { runSetup(tasks?.length ? tasks : []); })` — the deleted onMount (E0-3) is covered by the first apply. Options (:307-310): compute returns props.options, apply calls updateOptions. View mode (:313-327): delete the prevViewMode signal; `let prevViewMode = props.options?.viewMode;` and `createEffect(() => ({ viewMode: props.options?.viewMode, tasks: effectiveTasks() }), ({ viewMode, tasks }) => { if (viewMode && viewMode !== prevViewMode) { prevViewMode = viewMode; const win = dateStore.changeViewMode(viewMode); if (tasks?.length) runSetup(tasks, win); } })` — NO flush() here (silent no-op inside apply); the window returned by E1-3 is threaded into initializeTasks. Row-layout y-sync (:382-400): compute walks rowLayouts() into a plain `Array<[taskId, y]>`, apply does one `taskStore.setBarYs(pairs)` draft write (add that method to taskStore; skip entries whose draft y already matches). scrollTo:'start' (:502-520): compute returns `{ api, x: firstTask?._bar?.x }` plain, apply scrolls once. onReady (:234): `onSettled(() => { queueMicrotask(() => props.onReady?.(api)); })` so hosts may create primitives or call onCleanup in their callback (children-forbidden scope otherwise leaks into public API). Add a doc comment on GanttProps callbacks: they run untracked after the flush; store reads inside them see committed state.

Bar.tsx keyboard handler: `flush()` after the updateBarPosition at :300 and :311, before onDateChange/onResizeEnd. epics.title: Deferred-write and strict-read semantics in components, hooks, arrows and harnesses
epics.goal: Remove every remaining STRICT_READ storm, proxy leak into apply phases, hidden-dependency hack and same-tick latch that the audit found, and take the memo-laziness decision with measurements.
epics.rationale: None of these crash the shipped chart after E3, but they make the dev console unusable (ColumnPanel O(rows x tasks) warnings), silently render stale (arrow layers, SummaryBar memo), or change what the perf harnesses measure. Each is small and independently verifiable once E3-1 renders.
epics.verificationGate: pnpm dev with dev console: examples/custom-columns.html, gantt.html (hover popup + modal), perf-isolate.html?bar=full, experiments.html, index-test.html show zero STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED warnings during scroll and drag; pnpm test passes; pnpm build:demo passes.

children.title: ColumnPanel: row-level memo + inline cell expression (no store reads in For callback bodies); document ColumnDef.render purity
children.description: ColumnPanel.tsx:202 `const task = firstTaskForResource(item.id)` and :211-220 `const value = ...` read the task-store proxy inside `<For>` callback bodies, which carry a strict-read label in rc.6 -> STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED per cell per render, and the cells never updated when task data changed (pre-existing silent bug). Rewrite: `const task = createMemo(() => firstTaskForResource(item.id));` (creating a memo inside a For row is legal) and inline the cell expression into the JSX child: `{col.render ? col.render(task(), item.id) : ((task() as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.[col.key] ?? '')}`. Add to the exported ColumnDef type a doc comment: render(task, resourceId) is called inside a tracking scope on every dependency change; it must be pure and must not create primitives. Add a rule to the For-callback section of CLAUDE.md later (E7-1).
acceptance: pnpm dev examples/custom-columns.html: no STRICT_READ warnings on load or scroll; editing a task's name via console (`window.__ganttTaskStore.patchTask(id,{name:'x'}); `) updates the panel cell after the flush.

children.title: useGanttModals: snapshot() at the memo boundary; SummaryBar reads leaves; RowLayout/ConstraintContext invariants documented
children.description: useGanttModals.ts:45-63 memos return live store proxies (getTask) into TaskPopup/TaskModal, which would warn STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED if read inside an apply; wrap the four returns in `snapshot(...)` from solid-js (getBarPosition already allocates a plain object; give those two memos `{ equals: (a,b) => a?.x===b?.x && a?.y===b?.y && a?.width===b?.width && a?.height===b?.height }` so they do not notify every drag frame). SummaryBar.tsx:63 `createMemo(() => getPosition())` memoizes the raw _bar proxy — with leaf mutation (E1-1) it never invalidates; delete the memo and read fields directly like Bar.tsx:175-187. Add comments: RowLayout.taskPositions (rowLayoutCalculator.ts:10) and TaskLayer's Map<string, RowLayout> are memo outputs replaced wholesale, never mutated (built-ins are not proxied); ConstraintContext (types.ts:268) reads committed state and callers that wrote in the same tick must pass geometry explicitly (E1-4).
acceptance: pnpm dev examples/gantt.html: hover popup and click modal show current data; dragging a summary bar moves it visually every frame.
No STRICT_READ warnings when opening/closing the modal.

children.title: Memo laziness policy: measure mount cost, apply { lazy: true } only to measured rarely-read memos
children.description: rc.6 memos are eager and non-autodisposing by default; `{ lazy: true }` defers the first compute AND opts into autodisposal (teardown when unobserved, recompute on next read), which churns for virtualized bars (digest critic). Measure first: examples/perf.html at 10K tasks, mount time and scroll frame time (chrome-devtools-cli perf.mjs) with defaults vs with lazy on useBarConfig's 7 memos. Then apply lazy unconditionally only to genuinely rarely-read memos: useBarConfig showExpectedProgress/ignoredPositions/readonlyProgress, ganttDateStore getAllDateInfos (:303), the TaskDataModal/TaskDataPopup formatters that used to sit behind <Show>. Record numbers in the issue; keep everything else eager. Reference decision E0-1.
acceptance: Issue body has a before/after table (mount ms, avg/worst frame during scroll) for 10K tasks.
pnpm test and pnpm dev perf.html pass; no behavior change.

children.title: Arrow layers: real dependencies (no untrack key-set, no positionVersion counter), per-instance caches, regression test

Rewrite: read `Object.keys(tasks)` OUTSIDE untrack (or drop the untrack and let 2.0's flush coalesce), delete positionVersion and the GanttPerfIsolate.tsx:1529/1587 triggerArrowUpdate protocol, move the three caches into component scope threaded through spatialIndex's return value. Write the regression test first (jsdom project): mount ArrowLayer against a taskStore populated in the same synchronous run, flush(), assert positionMap is non-empty and updates after updateBarPosition + flush.

Where a harness times a RAF callback (index-test :1964 setOffset in an interval; GanttExperiments scroll tick), wrap the write in `flush(() => ...)`/call flush() at the end of the callback (legal in timers/RAF) so DOM work stays inside the measured frame, and say so in the harness header. memoTracker.js:136 createMemo initial value -> `{ loadingValue }` option. epics.title: Test hardening for deferred-write semantics
epics.goal: Pin the behaviors the migration fixed so they cannot regress: first-paint pipeline, delete semantics, expandedTasks reactivity, same-tick virtualization invalidation, drag-end geometry, view-mode regeneration, setter composition; optionally add component tests with diagnostics matchers.
epics.rationale: Chains A, C, G and H fail silently (no error, no warning). The existing suites cover none of them; the audit repeatedly asked for tests written before, not after, the risky change. Now that the jsdom client project exists (E2-1), hook-level synthetic-event tests are possible.

children.title: Regression suites: first-paint pipeline, removeTask delete, expandedTasks reactivity, same-tick add+remove grouping, drag-end geometry via synthetic events, changeViewMode window, makeSetter composition
children.description: Write with flush() after every write and no signal writes inside createRoot bodies (store writes are allowed there). (a) ganttSetup: fresh stores -> initializeTasks -> flush -> every task `_resourceIndex >= 0`, `_isHidden false`, `_bar.x` from its start date, dates().length > 0 (already added in E1-3; extend with the explicit-resources + collapsed-group path). (b) taskStore: removeTask then flush -> `Object.keys(store.tasks)` excludes the id; updateTasks then updateBarPosition on a new id in the SAME tick then flush -> position applied (guard-inside-draft). (c) ganttConfigStore: memo over expandedTasks() re-runs after toggleTaskExpansion + flush; collapse+expand in one tick ends expanded. (d) ganttDateStore: changeViewMode('Month') returns a window whose step/unit match and dates() (after flush) are monthly; extendTimeline('right') grows dates(). (e) useDrag + useBarDrag with a mock taskStore in jsdom: dispatch mousedown, `await Promise.resolve()`/flush(), mousemove, flush(), mouseup -> onDateChange receives the final geometry; the re-entrancy guard rejects a second mousedown in the same task. (f) useTaskVirtualization: remove one task and add another (same count) in one tick, flush -> grouping reflects the new set. (g) `setColumnWidth(w => w+10)` twice in one tick -> +20 (from E1-2). Each describe block names the chain it guards (A, B/C, G, J1, J2).
acceptance: All new suites pass under the client project; running them with the E1/E3 fixes reverted (locally, not committed) makes at least one assertion in each block fail.

Those redesigns are pure refactors on 1.9.12, so they go FIRST (E1), where the synchronous runtime and the existing dev-server smoke verify them for free and where each is its own revertable commit; by the time the runtime changes, the store layer no longer uses produce or path setters and the swap commit becomes a literal body move. E2-1 is the single unavoidable big commit and is kept mechanical by the demo shim; it depends on all of E0/E1 except the optional ConstraintDemo planner. openDecisions.question: Exact pins or caret ranges for the RC line (solid-js, @solidjs/web, @solidjs/vite-plugin, @solid-primitives/raf)?
openDecisions.recommendation: Exact pins for all four during the RC line; relax solid-js/@solidjs/web to ^2.0.0 only at stable via the E7-5 re-bump issue.
openDecisions.why: rc-to-rc changes have already altered write-guard semantics (createRoot exemption for stores only) and plugin test posture; a caret bump would silently invalidate the audit this plan is built on.

openDecisions.question: Feature branch or migrate on main?
openDecisions.recommendation: Feature branch `solid-2`, one commit per issue, merge with a merge commit after E6-5.
openDecisions.why: main must stay releasable on 1.9.12 (publish.yml triggers on the release branch); per-issue reverts and the stated window where the chart throws (between E2-1 and E3-1) belong on a branch.

openDecisions.question: Drop the UMD format or ship a self-contained bundle?
openDecisions.recommendation: Drop 'umd' in E2-1 (ESM-only; update package.json main/exports.require and README); file the self-contained IIFE bundle as an optional follow-up (E7-5d) only if a consumer asks.
openDecisions.why: Neither solid-js nor @solidjs/web publishes a global build, so the SolidJS/SolidJSWeb globals contract has no upstream artifact — the UMD output has been decorative and would emit missing-global warnings.

openDecisions.question: peerDependencies for solid-js and @solidjs/web now or later?
openDecisions.recommendation: Later (E7-5b), after merge; during migration keep them in dependencies with exact pins and add resolve.dedupe guidance to the README.
openDecisions.why: It is the correct library shape (two runtimes that must be the host's instance) but it changes consumers' install story; keeping it out of the migration keeps the branch's scope honest.

openDecisions.question: Keep or delete: taskStore collapse API, useGanttScroll isScrolling, dead ContainerAPI surface, GanttSubtaskDemo, duplicate onMount initializer?
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep the taskStore collapse API (exported public TaskStore type; collapsedTasks() is consumed by Gantt.tsx:294 and ganttSetup.ts:116; migrating its three tests costs ~20 lines). Delete isScrolling, the dead ContainerAPI surface, GanttSubtaskDemo and the duplicate onMount (E0-3/E0-4).
openDecisions.why: Only the collapse API is public and partially live; the rest has zero readers in src/ or tests/ and each is the hardest site in its file to migrate.

openDecisions.question: DbDemo modernization scope?
openDecisions.recommendation: Minimal in E3-4 (flush() first, captured x/width, functional TaskForm updaters, onSettled block body); actions/optimistic store + geometry-through-onDateChange as follow-up E7-5c.
openDecisions.why: The minimal fix closes the data-corruption chain H; the modernization is a public Gantt API addition and a demo rewrite, which the user asked to see as separate optional work.

openDecisions.question: Memo laziness policy ({ lazy: true } opts into autodisposal as well as deferral)?
openDecisions.recommendation: Eager by default; apply lazy only to the measured rarely-read memos in E4-3 (useBarConfig showExpectedProgress/ignoredPositions/readonlyProgress, getAllDateInfos, modal/popup formatters) after a 10K-task mount/scroll measurement.
openDecisions.why: Four audits recommended lazy without stating the autodisposal churn for virtualized bars; one measured decision across ~25 memos beats 25 local guesses.

openDecisions.question: expandedTasks representation: signal-held immutable Set or Record<string, true> inside the store?
openDecisions.recommendation: Signal-held immutable ReadonlySet (E1-2).
openDecisions.why: Matches the three existing safe instances (collapsedTasks, collapsedGroups, selectedIds), keeps the public option type Set<string> and rowLayoutCalculator's parameter unchanged, and is a 1.9-valid refactor; per-key granularity is not needed (every reader consumes the whole set).

openDecisions.question: Which demos lose @ts-nocheck?
openDecisions.recommendation: Strip it from the component/feature/db demos (Arrow, Bar, Constraint, Showcase, BoxSelect, MultiSelect, CriticalPath, FilterSearch, Export, CustomColumns, Gantt*, Db + db/*); keep it on the five perf harnesses and index-test.
openDecisions.why: tsc proves nothing behind @ts-nocheck, and the component demos are the ones that document the public contracts; the harnesses are 1-2K-line exploratory files whose typing cost is not migration work.

openDecisions.question: Add the optional @solidjs/testing-library and @solidjs/diagnostics devDependencies?
openDecisions.recommendation: Yes, as E5-2 (one component test file, exact pins), droppable if the beta misbehaves.
openDecisions.why: toHaveNoDiagnostics turns the migration's whole hazard class (write guard, strict-read storms, invalid cleanup returns) into one assertion on a bare <Gantt> mount, which no unit test can cover.

openDecisions.question: useGanttStores return type: keep GanttStores | undefined or switch to | null?
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep undefined via `useContext(Ctx) ?? undefined` (E2-1).
openDecisions.why: README.md:106 and Gantt.tsx:170 depend on it; zero public API churn.

plan.approachName: End-state idioms: reshape the data flow on 1.9 first, then one atomic runtime cutover, then 2.0-only refinements
principles: Producers return their computed values; consumers never read back state they just wrote (setupDates/changeViewMode return the window, batchMovePositions returns the applied map, drag handlers carry geometry in data). No flush() anywhere under src/ except demo code.

Every write lives in an event handler, an onSettled body, or the APPLY half of createEffect(compute, apply); compute returns PLAIN values (never store proxies) and apply has a block body (return-value trap).
Stores are draft-first with leaf mutation: taskStore mutates task._bar.x, never replaces state[id]; removal is delete draft[id]; existence guards live inside the draft where staged state is visible.
Built-in collections never live inside a createStore: expandedTasks joins collapsedTasks/collapsedGroups/selectedIds as a signal-held immutable Set; Dates inside stores are replace-only.

Derive instead of mirror: scroll/viewport are memos over the container's own signals; grouping and pool sizes are memos (prev-driven), not closure caches; isScrolling, positionVersion and the ContainerAPI debug surface are deleted, not ported.

Do the semantic work while still on solid-js 1.9 so the existing synchronous test suite proves it; the cutover commit is then almost purely mechanical (imports, lifecycle names, effect splitting, produce/path deletion).
Delete dead code instead of migrating it; strip // @ts-nocheck from every demo that is touched so tsc actually sees the 2.0 types.
One issue = one commit = one push. The only exception is the cutover, which is one issue precisely because it cannot be split without breaking the build.

Public API changes are confined to what the runtime forces (context defaults, void-returning config setters, useGanttStores(): GanttStores | null) and are each named in openDecisions; everything else (peerDependencies, UMD, DbDemo actions) is an explicit optional issue.
plan.branchStrategy: E1 (prune) and E2 (reshape) land on main: they are 1.9-compatible, each independently green (typecheck + lint + test + build + build:demo + dev smoke) and independently revertable, and they are worth having even if the RC line slips. E3 onward lands on a long-lived branch `solid-2.0` created from main after E2.8; every issue is one commit pushed to that branch. The branch is merged into main by fast-forward (rebase, no squash) after E5 and E6.1 are green so the one-issue-one-commit history survives. The `release` branch (publish.yml trigger) is NOT touched until the follow-up re-bump issue (E7.4) lands on a stable Solid; if an RC package must be published, do it manually with `npm publish --tag next` (open decision).
plan.versionPolicy: Pin EXACT versions for the whole RC line: solid-js 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/web 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.38 (not next.35: next.38 matches @solidjs/compiler rc.6 and adds the mode !== 'test' guards), @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2 (devDependencies), jsdom ^25 (caret is fine, not a Solid package), optional @solidjs/testing-library 1.0.0-beta.3 and @solidjs/diagnostics 2.0.0-rc.6 exact. Exact pins because RC-to-RC diffs change runtime guards (the createRoot write asymmetry and onSettled return validation both changed between RCs) and a caret bump would silently move the test posture. Re-bump policy: issue E7.4 re-runs the full gate against the newest RC/stable, relaxes to caret (^2.0.0) only once solid-js 2.0.0 stable ships, and adds peerDependencies at that point if E7.5 was deferred. Stage only package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml (+ config files) in dependency commits; dist-demo is refreshed once at the end (bd memory when-checked-in-build-artifacts).

epics.title: Prune: delete dead code and unused dependencies while still on solid-js 1.9
epics.goal: Shrink the migration surface by deleting everything the audit proved has no consumer, so nothing dead is ported to 2.0.
epics.rationale: The hardest sites in useGanttScroll (isScrolling: write-in-compute + timer) and GanttContainer (debug surface, scrollTiming signal) have zero readers; ArrowLayer.tsx and GanttSubtaskDemo.tsx have no importer/entry; four @solid-primitives packages are unimported; the taskStore collapse API has no caller and no docs. epics.title: Reshape data flow into 2.0 idioms while still on solid-js 1.9
epics.goal: Convert every write-then-read-back pipeline into compute-then-apply, thread drag geometry as data, move stores to leaf-mutation semantics, and derive scroll/virtualization state, all verified by the existing synchronous test suite before the runtime changes.
epics.rationale: Every high-severity hazard in the digest (chains A, B, C, D, F, G, I, J1, J2, J3) is a data-flow shape, not a syntax problem, and every fix is expressible on 1.9. Doing it here means the cutover commit changes syntax only, and any behavioural regression is bisectable to a small 1.9 commit with a green suite on both sides.
epics.verificationGate: Per issue: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm prettier-check && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm build:demo; dev smoke of examples/gantt.html (first paint shows bars, drag/resize/progress report final geometry), examples/showcase.html, examples/subtask.html (expand/collapse), examples/perf.html (scroll).

children.title: ganttDateStore: pure window computation; setupDates/changeViewMode/extendTimeline return values and never read their own staged signals
children.description: Chain A and J1: setupDates (ganttDateStore.ts:140-196) writes setGanttStart/setGanttEnd at :152-154 and :193-194 then generateDates() (:201-216) reads ganttStart()/ganttEnd()/step()/unit() back; changeViewMode (:243-254) stages the mode then generateDates reads step()/unit() memos derived from it; extendTimeline (:221-238) does the same. Under deferred writes all three regenerate from stale inputs (first paint: empty dates; view switch: old granularity). Rewrite: (1) add module-level pure helpers `buildDates(start, end, step, unit): Date[]` and `computeDateWindow(tasks, mode, infinitePadding): DateWindow` where `DateWindow = { ganttStart, ganttEnd, unit, step, columnWidth, dates }` (columnWidth derived from mode exactly as the memo at :126-131 does); (2) `setupDates(tasks, mode = viewMode(), infinitePadding = false): DateWindow` = compute, then commit all signals from the locals, then return the window; (3) `changeViewMode(mode): DateWindow | null` resolves the ViewMode object, derives step/unit/columnWidth locally via dateUtils.parse_duration, commits, returns; (4) extendTimeline uses the already-captured stepVal/unitVal and the new boundary local; (5) public generateDates() stays as `buildDates(ganttStart(), ganttEnd(), step(), unit())` for standalone use. Mark getAllDateInfos (:303) with a comment that it becomes { lazy: true } in E4.2. Add tests/ganttDateStore.test.ts covering computeDateWindow (padding, alignment, empty input) and buildDates (step/unit) as pure functions plus setupDates' return value equals its committed signals.
acceptance: setupDates/changeViewMode return a DateWindow whose dates.length matches dates() after the call (test)
generateDates has no signal reads other than in the public zero-arg wrapper (code review)
pnpm test passes; examples/gantt.html renders the same timeline as before; switching viewMode in examples/showcase.html regenerates columns at the new granularity
children.notes: GanttDateStore interface gains return types; no removal.

children.title: ganttSetup: compute-then-apply pipeline with local resource index map and a single config write
children.description: Chain A: ganttSetup.ts:66 writes the date store then :69-73 and :75-84 read five accessors back; :101 writes resources then :102 reads the resourceIndexMap memo back, which on first run is an empty non-null Map so taskProcessor.ts:231-262 marks every task _resourceIndex -1 / _isHidden true and the first paint is blank. Rewrite initializeTasks as a function of plain inputs: signature `initializeTasks(rawTasks, stores, input: { hasExplicitResources: boolean; mode?: ViewMode; collapsedGroups: Set<string>; collapsedTasks?: Set<string>; layout: { headerHeight; barHeight; padding } })`. Body: `const win = dateStore.setupDates(rawTasks, input.mode)`; build `config` from win + input.layout; one `ganttConfig.updateOptions({ ganttStart: win.ganttStart, ganttEnd: win.ganttEnd, unit: win.unit, step: win.step, columnWidth: win.columnWidth })` instead of five makeSetter calls; extract the loop at resourceStore.ts:62-72 into a pure `buildResourceIndexMap(display: DisplayResource[]): Map<string, number>` in resourceProcessor.ts used by both the store memo and ganttSetup; in the extraction branch compute `buildResourceIndexMap(computeDisplayResources(normalizeResources(extracted), input.collapsedGroups))` locally and still call resourceStore.updateResources(extracted) purely as a commit; in the explicit branch compute the same from resourceStore.resources() (committed, not written this turn). Strengthen tests/ganttSetup.test.ts: first-run assertion that no processed task has _isHidden true or _resourceIndex -1 and that bar x is computed against the task bounds (not today), plus resource-extraction assertions unchanged.
acceptance: initializeTasks reads no dateStore accessor and no resourceStore memo after writing them (code review: zero reads of dateStore.* / resourceStore.resourceIndexMap after line 66)
New first-run test passes on 1.9 and (after E3.1 with flush()) on 2.0
examples/gantt.html and examples/resource-groups.html first paint identical to before
children.notes: The empty-input branch (:56-63) also becomes a single commit sequence: clear(), setupDates([], mode), updateResources([]).

children.title: taskStore: leaf mutation, delete-on-remove, guards inside the draft, patch-merge updates, batchMovePositions returns applied positions
children.description: Rewrite every mutator so the cutover only deletes the word produce. updateBarPosition (:104-121): remove the committed-state guard at :108; inside the produce draft do `const t = state[id]; if (!t?._bar) return; for (const k in position) if (position[k] !== undefined) t._bar[k] = position[k];` (leaf mutation, no object replacement; the gantt-6hx cause #2 is that a memo returning the _bar proxy never invalidates, and Bar.tsx:175-187 already reads leaves). batchMovePositions (:156-173): leaf-mutate `t._bar.x = originalX + deltaX` and RETURN `Map<string, number>` of applied x values (chain D needs them). removeTask (:133-135): `setTasks(produce(s => { delete s[id]; }))` (in 2.0 assigning undefined keeps the key). updateTask (:99-101) becomes a patch-merge `updateTask(id, patch: Partial<ProcessedTask>)` via Object.assign inside the draft (ShowcaseDemo/useBarDrag build whole-node replacements from stale spreads), plus `setTaskProgress(id, p)` and `setBarYs(pairs: Array<[string, number]>)` (one draft write for Gantt's y-sync). Optional `createTaskStore(initialTasks?: ProcessedTask[])` so demos can be born populated. Tests: strengthen the gantt-6hx guard at tests/taskStore.test.ts:85-103 with a sibling memo on store.tasks['t1']?.name whose run count must stay 1 after updateBarPosition; add removeTask key-deletion (Object.keys length) test; add updateTask-then-updateBarPosition-same-turn test (guard must see the staged task); batchMovePositions return value test.
acceptance: tests/taskStore.test.ts contains the negative assertion (name memo runs stay 1) and it passes
grep 'state\[id\] = {' src/stores/taskStore.ts returns nothing

children.notes: TaskStore interface changes: updateTask patch semantics (callers ShowcaseDemo, useBarDrag updated in E2.5/E5.2), new setTaskProgress/setBarYs, batchMovePositions return type.

children.title: ganttConfigStore: expandedTasks becomes a signal-held immutable Set; setters become void-returning draft writes
children.description: expandedTasks is a Set created inside createStore (ganttConfigStore.ts:54, :146) and mutated in place through produce at :172-203; 2.0 does not proxy built-ins, so expand/collapse would notify nothing (Gantt.tsx:371 rowLayouts and useTaskVirtualization.ts:161 go dead). Move it out of the store into `createSignal<ReadonlySet<string>>(new Set(options.expandedTasks ?? []))`, matching taskStore.collapsedTasks/resourceStore.collapsedGroups/selectionStore.selectedIds; toggle/expand/collapse/expandAll/collapseAll become functional updaters that return a fresh Set; delete the committed-read early returns at :186 and :196 (replace-based updaters are idempotent); setExpandedTasks is the real signal setter; updateOptions (:214-257) routes expandedTasks to the signal; getConfig (:260-281) reads the signal. makeSetter (:151-166) reads committed state for prev and returns state[key] after the write, both wrong under deferral: reimplement as `setState(produce(d => { d[key] = typeof v === 'function' ? v(d[key]) : v; }))` returning void, and retype the 20 interface members (:81-100) from Setter<T> to `ConfigSetter<T> = (v: T | ((prev: T) => T)) => void`. Add a comment block in types.ts next to :198 (ProcessedTask Date fields) and :352 (expandedTasks option) stating the invariant: built-ins inside stores are replace-only. New tests/ganttConfigStore.test.ts: memo over expandedTasks() re-runs on toggle; two updater-form setColumnWidth calls compose (+20).

children.title: Drag contract: geometry travels as data from onDragMove to onDragEnd, resize cascades take explicit geometry, useDrag/useBoxSelect gate on plain locals
children.description: Chains B, C, D, H, J3. useDrag.handleMouseUp (useDrag.ts:154-187) runs the final onDragMove (:160-163, writes) then onDragEnd (:177, reads back) in one stack. Fix at the boundary, not with flush(): (1) useDrag keeps `let current: DragState = 'idle'` as the synchronous truth written next to every setDragState (:183, :218), every internal guard (:79, :84, :130, :155, :161, :177) reads `current`, the re-entrancy guard at :196 becomes `if (dragData) return;`, and isDragging collapses to `createMemo(() => dragState() !== 'idle')`; (2) useBarDrag stashes what it wrote into drag data: data.finalX/finalWidth at :164, :196-199, :208 (and the batch path :149 stores batchMovePositions' returned map), data.finalProgress at :252 using taskStore.setTaskProgress instead of the whole-node read-modify-write at :250-255; onDragEnd (:259-283) reports from data (delete the comment at :270 and the getBarPosition read at :271; :281 reports data.finalProgress); (3) widen the internal contract: Bar/SummaryBar props `onResizeEnd(taskId, geom: { x: number; width: number })` and SummaryBar `onDragEnd(taskId, geom)` (final x = originalX + deltaX); TaskLayer.handleResizeEnd(taskId, geom) (:98-102) forwards to `resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx, geom)` (taskLayerConstraints.ts:83-105) which uses geom instead of getBarPosition at :87; Bar keyboard resize (Bar.tsx:296-302) passes { x: x(), width: newWidth }; constrainTaskPosition (:54-77) keeps its per-frame read (frames are separate tasks) but takes the width from the caller when provided. (4) useBoxSelect: add `let passedThreshold = false` next to :94-98, set at :117-126, read at :135-137 instead of overlay(); keep the hit box in a plain local. Gantt's public onDateChange/onResizeEnd payloads are unchanged.

children.title: useGanttScroll derives from the container: memos over containerApi(), no mirror effects, dimensions seeded at mount
children.description: Showstopper (b) and chain I: handleContainerReady (useGanttScroll.ts:50-98) creates effects from a callback that will fire inside onSettled (children-forbidden) and reads api.getContainerWidth() (:52) one flush stale. Replace the hook with `useGanttScroll(containerApi: Accessor<ContainerAPILike | null>)` whose body is four memos: `scrollLeft = createMemo(() => containerApi()?.scrollLeftSignal() ?? 0)` and likewise scrollTop/viewportWidth/viewportHeight; delete handleContainerReady from GanttScroll (:35-36) and the batch import (:14); make the four signal members of ContainerAPILike required. GanttContainer.tsx:172 also seeds setViewportHeight(scrollAreaRef.clientHeight) so the mount path does not depend on the ResizeObserver. Gantt.tsx:248 becomes `useGanttScroll(containerApi)`; handleContainerReady (:489-497) shrinks to setContainerApi(api); the scrollTo:'today' branch (:494-497) moves into an effect gated on containerApi() and scroll.viewportWidth() > 0 that fires once (plain `let todayDone`), and the scrollTo:'start' effect (:502-519) uses `firstTask?._bar?.x !== undefined` instead of truthiness.

children.title: Virtualization and ColumnPanel derive: tracked grouping memo (shared helper), prev-driven pool sizes, row-level memo in ColumnPanel
children.description: Chain G: the grouping cache keyed on task COUNT (useTaskVirtualization.ts:70-96, duplicated at TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:45-73) goes permanently stale once 2.0 coalesces a same-tick add+remove; the pool high-water counters (:201-232) are mutable state inside memo computes. Rewrite: extract `groupTasksByResource(tasks: TaskMap): Map<string, ProcessedTask[]>` (reads Object.keys plus each task's _isHidden and resource TRACKED, no untrack) into taskProcessor.ts and wrap it in a createMemo in both consumers; delete the closure caches. Pool sizes become memos with prev: `const regularPoolSize = createMemo((prev: number = 0) => Math.max(prev - POOL_BUFFER, splitTaskIds().regularIds.length) + POOL_BUFFER)` (1.x and 2.0 both pass prev), and pooledRegularIds/pooledSummaryIds read it. useTaskVirtualization.ts:161 reads props.ganttConfig.expandedTasks() as an explicit dependency outside the untrack at :152. ColumnPanel.tsx:202 snapshots a store proxy in the For callback body and :211 per cell (STRICT_READ storm in 2.0 and a live non-reactivity bug today): wrap the row lookup in `const task = createMemo(() => firstTaskForResource(item.id))` inside the callback and inline the cell expression into JSX; document in the ColumnDef type that render(task, resourceId) runs inside a tracking scope and must be pure. Measure the tracked grouping on examples/perf.html 10K (subscription count is O(N) but re-runs only on structure changes); if mount time regresses more than 10%, fall back to a `taskStore.structureVersion` signal bumped by updateTasks/updateTask/removeTask/clear and read leaves untracked.

children.title: Gantt.tsx consumes the pipeline: runSetup(input), duplicate onMount deleted, single-write y-sync, plain prevViewMode
children.description: Chain A/F/J1 orchestration on 1.9 (syntax split happens in E3.1). epics.title: Cutover: solid-js 2.0.0-rc.6 runtime, tooling, and all mechanical syntax in one commit
epics.goal: Swap the runtime and every removed/renamed API in a single buildable commit, with the test suite running in the correct client/server Vitest posture.
epics.rationale: The dependency swap and the import/lifecycle rewrites cannot be separated without breaking typecheck or build (solid-js/web, solid-js/store, onMount, Index, produce, batch, createComputed all vanish at once). E2 has already removed every semantic decision, so this commit is large but mechanical, and a rehearsal issue enumerates the exact error inventory first.
epics.verificationGate: pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm prettier-check && pnpm test (client and server projects both green) && pnpm build; pnpm dev smoke of every example whose demo is NOT // @ts-nocheck: gantt, subtask, resource-groups, box-select, multi-select, export, filter-search, critical-path, custom-columns with zero Solid diagnostics in the console. EXPLICITLY RED until E5.1: pnpm build:demo and the @ts-nocheck demo pages (perf, perf-isolate, experiments, minimal-test, profiler, index-test, showcase, constraint, bar, arrow, db).

epics.title: Library end-state on 2.0: positional pools, measured memo laziness, diagnostics-clean mount, arrow layer without manual dependency protocols
epics.goal: Adopt the 2.0-only primitives and policies that could not be expressed on 1.9, with measurements recorded so nothing is a guess.
epics.rationale: Repeat is the native fit for the fixed-slot pools that Index emulated; eager memos change per-Bar mount cost; STRICT_READ warnings at 10K rows make dev unusable and skew profiles; the arrow layer's untrack/positionVersion protocol reimplements what the 2.0 scheduler now does.

children.title: Replace the three sparse-array pools with <Repeat count={poolSize()}> and verify drag survives pool reuse
children.description:
The pools feed sparse arrays (`new Array(poolSize)` with holes); hole semantics under the new reconciler are unproven and the audit flagged it as load-bearing (a remount tears down Bar's document listeners mid-drag). Repeat is the store-backed positional primitive: `{(i) =>
pooledRegularTasks()[i]} .../>
}` at TaskLayer.tsx:249-268, likewise the summary pool at :217-230 and TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:130. Rows in the overlapping index range are preserved when count grows, so the never-shrink pool semantics hold. pooledRegularIds/pooledSummaryIds return dense arrays. Bar.tsx:110-118 getTask keeps the value-or-accessor handling (the accessor is now a plain closure over the memo). Benchmark with benchmarks/scripts/run-virt.sh against the For keyed={false} build from E3.1 and keep Repeat if scroll fps and mount are at parity or better.

children.description: Chain H: onDateChange (DbDemo.tsx:146) runs inside the mouseup stack and reads taskStore.tasks[id]._bar (:195-196) one frame stale, persists short deltas, then re-bases from the committed value after the await (:239-242) so the error compounds. openDecisions.question: Exact pins or caret for the RC line?
openDecisions.recommendation: Exact pins (2.0.0-rc.6, 3.0.0-next.38, 4.0.0-next.2); caret only at stable via E7.4.
openDecisions.why: RC-to-RC changes altered dev guards (createRoot write asymmetry, onSettled return validation, vite-plugin test posture); a caret bump would silently change test semantics.

openDecisions.question: Feature branch or main?
openDecisions.recommendation: E1/E2 on main (1.9-compatible, independently valuable); E3 onward on branch solid-2.0, fast-forward merged after E5 + E6.1.
openDecisions.why: The cutover leaves build:demo red for a few commits and the RC should not reach the release branch; the prep work is safe on main and keeps main useful if the RC slips.

openDecisions.question: Drop UMD or ship a self-contained bundle?
openDecisions.recommendation: Drop umd: formats ['es'], main/module/exports on the es build, remove the require condition.
openDecisions.why: Neither solid-js nor @solidjs/web publishes a global build, so the UMD contract was already decorative; a self-contained bundle would duplicate the reactive runtime in consumers.

openDecisions.question: peerDependencies for solid-js and @solidjs/web?
openDecisions.recommendation: Yes, as optional issue E7.5 (peer + dev), not inside the cutover.
openDecisions.why: Two externalized runtimes must be the host app's instance; this is a packaging change the user should approve separately.

openDecisions.question: Delete or keep: taskStore collapse API, isScrolling, ContainerAPI debug surface, ArrowLayer.tsx, GanttSubtaskDemo.tsx?
openDecisions.recommendation: Delete all five (E1.1, E1.2, E1.4); the taskStore collapse API is decision-gated because it is reachable via the exported TaskStore type.
openDecisions.why: None has a library caller or documentation (docs/SUBTASKS.md documents ganttConfig.collapseTask, a different API); porting them is where the hardest sync hazards and the createRoot signal-write test problem live.

openDecisions.question: DbDemo modernization scope?
openDecisions.recommendation: Migration scope = settle-then-diff via onSettled and recorded deltas (E5.4); actions/createOptimisticStore is backlog E7.6.
openDecisions.why: onSettled from the mouseup handler reads committed geometry including cascades with no flush() and no library API change; the async-model rewrite is a demo feature, not a migration need.

openDecisions.question: Lazy memo policy?
openDecisions.recommendation: Measured, minimal: lazy only for rarely-read memos (three useBarConfig memos, modal/popup formatters, getAllDateInfos); everything else eager (E4.2).
openDecisions.why: lazy also opts into autodispose-and-recompute, which for virtualized bars trades mount cost for churn; the per-bar hot memos are always read.

openDecisions.question: expandedTasks representation: signal-held Set or Record<string, true> in the store?
openDecisions.recommendation: Signal-held immutable Set (E2.4).
openDecisions.why: Matches the three existing collections, keeps the public accessor/option types and rowLayoutCalculator untouched; the per-key tracking a Record would give is unused (the consumer reads inside untrack).

openDecisions.question: Pool primitive: <For keyed={false}> or <Repeat>?
openDecisions.recommendation: For keyed={false} in the cutover (identical callback shape, zero risk), Repeat in E4.1 if benchmarks are at parity.
openDecisions.why: Repeat is the native positional pool and avoids sparse-array semantics, but its reconciler behaviour must be measured before it carries the drag-listener invariant.

openDecisions.question: useGanttStores return type: undefined (via ?? undefined) or null?
openDecisions.recommendation: null; update README:106.
openDecisions.why: createContext<T | null>(null) is the documented optional-provider form; a `?? undefined` shim only preserves a type nobody depends on (Gantt.tsx:170 uses ??).

openDecisions.question: Adopt @solidjs/testing-library and @solidjs/diagnostics?
openDecisions.recommendation: Yes, both (dev-only, exact pins); E4.3/E6.1 use toHaveNoDiagnostics as the chain A guard.
openDecisions.why: A diagnostics-clean mount test is the only automated proof for the silent-failure classes; cost is two devDependencies.

openDecisions.question: Publish RC builds to npm?
openDecisions.recommendation: Not to latest; either hold or publish with --tag next (E7.5).
openDecisions.why: Consumers on 1.x would receive a breaking runtime from a caret update.

openDecisions.question: gitignore dist-demo instead of refreshing it?
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep tracked and refresh once (E7.1) for this migration; revisit with E7.5.
openDecisions.why: The bench scripts serve it; changing the artifact policy is orthogonal scope.

bestIdeas: Do all the semantic reshaping on solid-js 1.9 first (E2), where the existing synchronous suite still verifies it, so the runtime swap is almost purely mechanical and any behavioural regression bisects to a small green commit. This is the single best structural decision in the plan.

Adopt the digest's one architectural rule instead of ~15 site fixes: producers return their computed values (setupDates/changeViewMode return a DateWindow, batchMovePositions returns the applied map), consumers never read back what they just wrote, and store existence guards move inside the draft. Directly implements the tracer's CROSS finding.

E1 first: delete isScrolling, the dead ContainerAPI debug surface, ArrowLayer.tsx and GanttSubtaskDemo.tsx before migrating. This removes two of the six scroll hazards, one primitive from a children-forbidden scope, and the top arrow hazard at zero cost.

taskStore leaf mutation (t._bar.x = v) with the *negative* regression assertion (a sibling memo on tasks['t1'].name whose run count must stay 1). Without that assertion nothing prevents someone porting the 1.x object-replacement shape into the draft, which compiles and passes the old test while keeping the cost.
Deferring consumer callbacks out of onSettled with queueMicrotask (onReady) so the children-forbidden contract never propagates into user code — exactly the critic's shared rule.

The E3.0 rehearsal in a throwaway worktree producing the exact tsc error inventory and answers to five concrete runtime questions before the XL cutover. Cheap, and the deliberate no-commit exception is well justified.

One shared src/demo/perfHarness.ts (useViewportSize/useRafLoop/createLatch) replacing five copy-pasted onMount+ResizeObserver+RAF bodies and seven read-then-write latches, per the digest's two CROSS findings.

Split-effect derivation (compute returns a plain object, apply has a block body) as the fix for the one architectural defect shared by ShowcaseDemo/ConstraintDemo/DbDemo, rather than three independent flush() patches.
Stripping // @ts-nocheck from every demo that is touched, with 'page runs with zero diagnostics' as the acceptance — the only way the type-level half of the migration becomes visible in those files.
Exact version pins for the whole RC line with a single re-bump issue (E7.4) as the only place versions move, justified by RC-to-RC guard changes.
The openDecisions block itself: 13 named decisions with recommendation + rationale, each tied to an issue, is the right shape for keeping the user out of scope-creep surprises.
dist-demo refreshed exactly once as its own 'chore(demo): refresh built artifacts' commit, with the benchmark re-baseline sequenced against it and old tables date-stamped rather than deleted.
review.summary: Strong plan and the best available skeleton for the migration: it correctly identifies that the hard work is data-flow shape (not syntax), does that work on 1.9 where the existing suite still proves it, deletes dead code first, and it has clearly absorbed the critics' runtime corrections (onSettled untracked, queueMicrotask for onReady, block bodies for return-value validation, signal-vs-store createRoot asymmetry, no flush in apply/onSettled). The defects are concentrated in the cutover issue and the tail. E3.1 cannot pass its own gates as written: its test list omits the two suites E2.1/E2.4 create, its vitest client include glob (tests/*.test.ts) will silently skip the .tsx suites E4.3/E6.1 add, its acceptance grep covers src/entries while index-test.tsx is assigned to E5.1 (verified: 4 Index sites, 2 Provider tags, a solid-js/store import), and it claims 10 client suites where the repo has 14. Two issues use an invalid bd type (decision). Coverage gaps are real but bounded: SummaryBar.tsx:63's memo-over-proxy silently stops invalidating the moment E2.3 lands leaf mutation; ganttConfigStore's unproxied Dates (verified at GanttConfigState:35/36/48) are handed raw to consumer updaters by the E2.4 setter rewrite; resourceStore.collapseAll and (in the recommended delete branch) taskStore.collapseAllTasks keep their read-then-write; useGanttModals still leaks store proxies. Ordering: the lint/tsconfig glob widening lands after the commit that rewrites the config files it would have covered, ci.yml is gated to a window where build:demo is red by design, and the entire tail (artifacts, benchmarks, docs, memories) blocks on an optional arrow refinement. Fix those and this is the plan to build the synthesis around.

plan.approachName: Verification-first migration: pin behavior on 1.9, flip atomically on a branch, turn every red test green one issue at a time
principles: Every behavioral change ships with a test that is red on the parent commit and green on the fix commit; the flip commit's test report IS the regression inventory.
Characterization tests are written on solid-js 1.9 (main) using a tests/helpers/settle() that is a no-op on 1.9 and becomes flush() at the flip, so timing edits never mix with behavioral edits.

Producers return their computed values; consumers never read back state they just wrote; store guards move inside the draft. flush() only in event handlers/timers/test bodies (no-op in effect apply, throws in onSettled).

Test posture is fixed before any reactive test is touched: Vitest projects (client=jsdom for tests/*.ts[x], server=node for tests/server/*), no signal writes inside createRoot bodies (store writes are exempt), DEV.diagnostics capture gate with zero error/warn events.
One issue -> one commit -> one push, except the flip (E2.1-E2.4) which is one commit because the build cannot pass between them. Feature branch solid-2; main stays green throughout.
Migrate, do not port: the gantt-6hx object-replacement hack becomes leaf mutation guarded by a negative assertion; untrack-hidden dependencies and count-keyed caches are replaced, not translated.

Every callback handed to onSettled/createEffect apply or invoked from them gets a block body (rc.6 throws on non-function return values). Consumer callbacks (onReady, onContainerReady, onSelectionChange) are never called synchronously from an onSettled body.
Scope creep is opt-in: UMD, peerDependencies, dead-code deletion, DbDemo modernization and lazy-memo policy are explicit decisions or optional issues, never folded into a required one.
plan.branchStrategy: E0 (gates + Vitest projects) and E1 (characterization tests) land on main first: they are green on solid-js 1.9.12 and give main the regression net before any runtime changes. Create branch `solid-2` from that point. E2 (flip) through E5 land on `solid-2` as one commit per issue; the flip commit is allowed to have the enumerated failing characterization tests (the issue lists them by name) because main is untouched. Merge `solid-2` into main with a merge commit (not squash, to keep one-issue-one-commit history) only when the end-of-migration verification plan is fully green; the dist-demo refresh commit (E5.4) is the last commit on the branch before merge. CI publish.yml runs only on `release`, so add typecheck/lint/test there in E0.1 so the eventual release push is gated.
plan.versionPolicy: Exact pins (no caret) for the whole RC line while on rc.6: solid-js 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/web 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.38 (matches @solidjs/compiler rc.6; next.35 lacks the mode!=='test' guards), @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2 (devDependencies), @solidjs/diagnostics 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/testing-library 1.0.0-beta.3 (only if adopted), jsdom ^25. Rationale: RCs break each other across patch numbers and the audit's runtime facts were verified against rc.6 specifically. Re-bump is its own issue (E6.5): move all five to the newest RC/stable together, re-run the full verification plan, then relax solid-js/@solidjs/web to caret (and to peerDependencies if that decision is taken). pnpm: add @solidjs/compiler to pnpm-workspace.yaml onlyBuiltDependencies only if `pnpm install` reports a blocked build script; verify `pnpm ls solid-js @solidjs/web` shows exactly one version each.

children.title: Gantt.tsx effect splits: setup/options/view-mode/selection/row-sync; delete duplicate onMount; onReady via onSettled + queueMicrotask
children.description: All writes reached from effect COMPUTES throw REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (untrack does not clear the owner): Gantt.tsx:298/302/324 runSetup, :309 updateOptions, :320-321 setPrevViewMode/changeViewMode, :395 updateBarPosition, :184-188 props.onSelectionChange. (1) Delete the onMount at :288 (duplicate of the :290 effect; under one flush window it reads its own uncommitted writes). (2) Setup effect -> `createEffect(() => { const tasks = effectiveTasks(); resourceStore.collapsedGroups(); taskStore.collapsedTasks(); return tasks; }, (tasks) => { runSetup(tasks?.length ? tasks : []); })`. (3) Options effect -> compute returns props.options, apply calls updateOptions (block body). (4) View-mode effect -> plain `let prevViewMode` (not a signal); compute returns {viewMode, tasks}; apply: if changed, `const win = dateStore.changeViewMode(viewMode)` and pass `win` into runSetup/initializeTasks so no flush() is needed (flush() inside apply is a silent no-op — critic DISPUTED Gantt.tsx:316). (5) Selection effect -> compute returns `Array.from(selectionStore.selectedIds())`, apply `(ids) => { props.onSelectionChange?.(new Set(ids)); }` block body. (6) Row-sync effect :382-400 -> compute returns a plain `Array<[id, y]>` from rowLayouts(), apply performs ONE `setTasks(draft => ...)` leaf write of _bar.y (chain F), or delete the effect and feed rowLayouts to useBoxSelect if decision D9 says so. (7) `onMount(() => props.onReady?.(api))` -> `onSettled(() => { queueMicrotask(() => props.onReady?.(api)); })` so consumers keep full freedom (no children-forbidden leakage); document. (8) Gantt.tsx:515 `firstTask?._bar?.x !== undefined`. (9) Wrap the 7 deliberate one-shot props reads in untrack if E2.2 did not.

openDecisions.question: D1: Exact pins or caret for the RC line?
openDecisions.recommendation: Exact pins (2.0.0-rc.6 / 3.0.0-next.38 / 4.0.0-next.2 / diagnostics rc.6) until E6.5; then caret.
openDecisions.why: The audit's runtime facts (write guard asymmetry, onSettled untracked, return-value validation) were verified against rc.6 specifically; RC-to-RC drift would silently invalidate the tests' assumptions.

openDecisions.question: D2: Feature branch or main?
openDecisions.recommendation: E0+E1 on main (green on 1.9), then branch solid-2 for E2-E6, merge commit when fully green.
openDecisions.why: The flip commit necessarily has failing characterization tests and a non-functional chart; main must stay releasable and the tests should exist before the branch so main gets the regression net immediately.

openDecisions.question: D3: Drop UMD or ship a self-contained bundle?
openDecisions.recommendation: Drop 'umd' from formats, keep 'es' only; point package.json main/exports.require at the ES build (or remove require); note in README.
openDecisions.why: Neither solid-js nor @solidjs/web publishes a global/IIFE build, so the UMD globals contract has been decorative and doubles now; a self-contained bundle is scope creep (E6.6) unless a UMD consumer is known.

openDecisions.question: D4: peerDependencies for solid-js/@solidjs/web?
openDecisions.recommendation: Not in this migration; keep exact pins in dependencies, add a resolve.dedupe note to README, and revisit in E6.5/E6.6.

openDecisions.recommendation: Delete isScrolling and the dead ContainerAPI surface in E3.2 (they are the hardest scroll sites to migrate and have zero readers); delete the taskStore collapse API in E3.6 (tests-only consumer; removes the only createRoot signal-write problem); delete GanttSubtaskDemo (no entry) and the six already-broken variants in E4.5/E4.6.

openDecisions.question: D6: expandedTasks representation: signal-held immutable Set or Record<string,true> in the store?
openDecisions.recommendation: Signal-held ReadonlySet with whole-Set replacement (public accessor type unchanged, matches the three existing safe patterns).
openDecisions.why: Consistency with taskStore.collapsedTasks/resourceStore.collapsedGroups/selectionStore.selectedIds and zero public type change; Record gives per-key tracking but rowLayouts reads the whole set anyway. Switch to Record only if E5 shows expand/collapse invalidation cost on 10K-task charts.

openDecisions.question: D7: Adopt @solidjs/testing-library for the mount tests?
openDecisions.recommendation: No; use render() from @solidjs/web + a mountGantt helper, and DEV.diagnostics.capture() for the gate; add @solidjs/diagnostics only for its Vitest matchers if they load under vitest 4.1.
openDecisions.why: The tests assert store state and SVG elements, not accessible roles; one fewer beta dependency on the RC line and the helper works on 1.9 for the pre-flip characterization.

openDecisions.question: D8: Lazy-memo policy?
openDecisions.recommendation: Default eager everywhere; { lazy: true } only on getAllDateInfos and the modal/popup formatters now; decide per-Bar memos from E5.2 measurements.
openDecisions.why: lazy also opts into autodisposal, which churns for virtualized rows; four audits recommended it without stating the second effect, so it must be measured, not guessed.

openDecisions.question: D9: Row-sync effect (Gantt.tsx:382-400): keep as a split effect writing _bar.y, or delete and feed rowLayouts to useBoxSelect?
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep as a split effect with one draft write in E3.5 (smallest change, keeps _bar.y for exported components); reconsider deletion in a follow-up.

review.summary: The strongest of the plans on runtime fidelity: it encodes the corrected facts (createRoot signal-vs-store asymmetry, flush's three scopes, onSettled untracked + children-forbidden, return-value validation, delete draft[id], unproxied Set, <For>'s strict-read label, null-default contexts) and its site coverage of the digests is close to complete, with real gates (grep sweeps, diagnostics capture, a negative gantt-6hx assertion, a For-pooling proof) rather than prose. Three things stop it being executable as written: E2.3's Index inventory misses DateHeadersOptimized/GanttMinimalTest/GanttPerfIsolate so the atomic flip commit cannot pass its own `pnpm build:demo` gate; E3.5 is ordered before the taskStore API (E3.6) it depends on; and E1's 'green on main' gate is contradicted by E1.5/E1.8 admitting red tests on 1.9. Secondary: the flip is one ~120-file commit that smuggles public-API changes under 'purely mechanical'; the same-turn view-mode path is not actually closed by E3.3-E3.5; E4.4 prescribes a store-proxy read in an effect apply that its own E4.8 gate forbids; and nothing in the plan produces the beads epic/issue tree the user asked for. Fix those and this is the plan to ship.
